Definition: third person singular imperative of G1510; let him (or it) be:--let … be.
BiblicalUsage: Ḗtō is the word for 'let him be' — the third-person imperative of the verb to be. It occurs twice: 'let him be Anathema' and 'let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay'. The form hands the matter over to what must be.
TheologicalSignificance: I take ḗtō as it stands — let it be — and I hear in it both a curse and a command to plain speech.
